sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.raw: The dominant story remains Thursday's weak June US jobs report (+57K vs. ~110K expected, prior months revised lower), which reopened Fed rate-cut pricing even as Chair Warsh talked tough on inflation at the ECB Forum in Sintra. That tension is colliding with a holiday-thinned session: US equity and bond markets are fully closed today for the July 4 holiday (observed, since the 4th falls on a Saturday), so liquidity is light into a long weekend. Dollar softness from the jobs miss is not showing up evenly — GBP is outperforming on hawkish BoE commentary while EUR stays capped — which muddies today's read. Treat any single-pair signal here as a watch item, not a trigger, until normal volume returns Monday.

| RBA | 4.35% | Held, Jun 2026 | Hawkish-hold; inflation still elevated |
| RBNZ | 2.25% | Held, May 2026 (3rd straight hold) | Neutral–dovish |

**Key divergence:** the ECB and BoJ are this cycle's hawkish outliers — the ECB's first hike since 2023 and the BoJ's continued normalization toward 1%+ — while the Fed, BoE, BoC, RBA, RBNZ, and SNB all sit on hold. A rare stretch where the traditionally dovish ECB and BoJ are out-hawking the Fed.

sections.title: Economic Catalyst Check
sections.raw: US cash equity and bond markets are **closed today** for the July 4 holiday (observed). No US red-folder releases scheduled today. June NFP already printed Thursday, July 2, 8:30am ET (+57K vs. ~110K expected) — a known driver already in the price, not a forward catalyst. Next scheduled high-impact items: **Eurozone Retail Sales (EUR)** and **US ISM Services PMI (USD)**, both Monday, July 6 — exact release times to confirm as the week opens (typically ~05:00 ET / 09:00 GMT for EZ retail sales, ~10:00 ET / 14:00 GMT for ISM Services).

sections.title: Scenario Watch
sections.raw:
- **GBP/USD:** If it holds above ~1.3300 into next week, that confirms the Bailey-driven hawkish BoE repricing; a fail back below 1.3300 points to the move fading as a one-day event spike.
- **AUD/USD:** If it clears ~0.6920, that confirms the RBA hawkish-hold carry trade extending; a rejection below ~0.6880 points to broader risk-off dragging it back down.
- **USD/CAD:** If it breaks above ~1.4220, that confirms the soft-oil/BoC-hold theme pushing CAD weaker; failure to hold above ~1.4180 points to oil stabilizing and capping the move.
